info.title: govhub relay API
info.description: A queue in front of a dashd. Accepts fully signed masternode governance FUNDING votes and broadcasts them with `voteraw`, immediately or at a client-chosen release time (deferred / randomized voting), and submits proposals: at once when the collateral is in a ChainLocked block or 6 deep (POST /v1/proposals/submit), or held until then, submitted by the relay itself and followed until Core has it in full at 6 confirmations (POST /v1/proposals). The relay holds no accounts, keeps no IP addresses at rest and only a coarse receive hour per vote. Its operator can see the IP and timing of every request: public unlinkability only. Votes are signed by the client with the masternode VOTING key (`signVote` in @govhub/verify); the relay never sees a key. The id returned by POST /v1/votes, not the vote hash, is the handle for status and cancel. CORS is open (origin *, GET/POST/OPTIONS, header content-type). Every response carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Every POST body is limited to 4096 bytes (413). Errors are `{error, code}` with a stable `code`.

get.description: Always 200 while the process serves HTTP (container health check). `core.reachable` says whether dashd answers; the answer is cached for 5 s.

post.description:
Checks, in this order: network (`wrong-network`), field types and unknown keys (`bad-request`), Core's relay rules via `relayVoteError` (`bad-vote`: funding only, outcome yes/no/abstain, time positive and at most MAX_HOLD_S ahead), the release time (`bad-release`; a signed `time` older than MAX_PAST_S, default 24 h, is `stale-vote`), the masternode (`unknown-mn`, `mn-banned`), the signature (`bad-signature`: the recovered key must be the masternode's current voting key; Core's non-strict recovery rules, i.e. any header byte and high-S), the proposal (`unknown-proposal`, `not-a-proposal`). A vote whose hash is already stored (in any state) returns 200 with the stored record: this is how a client whose POST got no answer (timeout) recovers the relay `id` and `status`, by sending the same signed vote again. There is deliberately no lookup by vote hash (a vote hash can be computed from public data, so it would let anyone confirm a held vote). Then Core is asked (`gobject getcurrentvotes`; a failing call is ignored): 409 `already-current` if Core already has this vote hash as the masternode's current vote, 409 `newer-vote-in-core` if it has a funding vote of this masternode dated at or after this one; neither is queued or counted against any limit. A held vote of the same masternode on the same proposal is superseded by one with a greater `time` and refused otherwise (`later-vote-held`). Then the limits, which only votes that are really queued count against: per masternode per rolling hour (`rate-limited`), held votes per masternode (`too-many-held`) and held votes in total (503 `relay-full`, MAX_HELD_TOTAL). The per-IP token bucket (`rate-limited`, Retry-After) applies to every POST before the body is read.

The vote is released at `releaseAt` (default: max(now, time - RELEASE_MARGIN_S)); an explicit `releaseAt` must satisfy time - 3540 <= releaseAt <= time + 86400 and releaseAt <= now + MAX_HOLD_S, and a value in the past means now.

200.description: this exact vote (same vote hash) is already stored; its current record

post.description: `sig` is the masternode's CURRENT voting key signing (Dash `signmessage`, DarkCoin message magic, the same scheme on every network) the text `govhub-relay-cancel-v1\n<network>\n<vote hash, lowercase display hex>` (relayCancelMessage in @govhub/verify). A held vote becomes `cancelled`; cancelling a cancelled vote is a no-op 200. A vote any attempt of which may have reached Core (`maybeSent`: `maybe-broadcast`, or `sending` / `failed` after such an attempt) is 409 `maybe-broadcast` with the vote's `status` and a `reason` the client can show: it cannot be taken back. Any other state is 409 `not-held` with the vote's `status`; `sending` (voteraw in flight) is one of them.

409.description: `not-held`: the vote already left the held state. `maybe-broadcast`: an earlier attempt may have reached Core, so the vote cannot be cancelled; `reason` says so in plain words

reason.description: `maybe-broadcast` only: a sentence for the user

get.description: Votes in a final state are deleted RETENTION_DAYS after they finished; the id is then unknown.

post.summary: Submit a proposal to Core (`gobject submit`)
post.description: Stateless; still supported (see POST /v1/proposals for a relay that waits for the confirmations itself). 501 `disabled` when the relay runs with PROPOSAL_SUBMIT=0. Everything is verified again before Core is asked: the proposal data (`validateProposalData`, `bad-proposal`), the gov hash, and the collateral transaction fetched from Core (`checkCollateralTx` against that hash and the named txid, `bad-collateral`). A collateral is submittable with at least MIN_COLLATERAL_CONFS (default 1) confirmations in a block a ChainLock covers (`chainlock` from `getrawtransaction`), or with 6 confirmations without one; otherwise 425 `collateral-unconfirmed` with the current `confirmations` and `chainlock`. Below 6 confirmations Dash Core accepts the object as postponed: it relays it at once and makes it a full (live, votable) object when the collateral is 6 deep (`postponed: true` in the answer). This endpoint does not follow up: Core keeps a postponed object in memory only, so a restart of the relay's dashd before 6 confirmations loses the relay's own copy (peers keep theirs); POST /v1/proposals checks again at 6 and submits again if needed. Core's refusal is 409 `core-rejected` carrying Core's message (proposal data is public).

425.description: the collateral transaction is not ChainLocked or deep enough yet

chainlock.description: a ChainLock covers the collateral's block (Core's `getrawtransaction` flag)

post.summary: Hold a proposal until its collateral is ChainLocked, then submit it (`gobject submit`) and follow it to 6 confirmations
post.description: For clients that cannot stay online after paying: the relay stores the proposal and submits it itself once Core's `getrawtransaction <txid> true` shows at least MIN_COLLATERAL_CONFS (default 1) confirmations with `chainlock: true`, or 6 confirmations without a ChainLock. Below 6 Dash Core keeps the object postponed (in memory only) and relays it at once; it becomes a full, votable object at 6. So the record stays `waiting` with `sent: true` until the collateral is 6 deep and `gobject get` shows Core has the object; if Core lost it (a dashd restart), the relay submits it again. Only then is it `submitted`. Same body as /v1/proposals/submit, validated identically, in this order: 501 `disabled` (PROPOSAL_SUBMIT=0), `bad-request` (not a JSON object), `wrong-network`, `bad-request` (unknown keys, types), `bad-proposal` (`validateProposalData` with the current time, i.e. Core's ValidateProposal including end_epoch in the future). Then a proposal already stored under the same (gov hash, collateral txid) returns 200 with its record in any state, without asking Core (this is how a client recovers the `id` after a timeout). Then the limits: 409 `too-many-collaterals` (at most 3 records per gov hash, any state) and 503 `relay-full` (MAX_HELD_PROPOSALS waiting and submitting records). Then the collateral is fetched from Core: 404 `unknown-collateral` if Core does not know the transaction (retry: it may not have propagated yet), 503 `core-unavailable`, 400 `bad-collateral` (with `failure`) unless `checkCollateralTx` passes against the computed gov hash and the named txid (P2PKH/unspendable outputs only, an OP_RETURN of the hash worth >= 1 DASH). A collateral still in the mempool is fine. A new record is 202: `waiting`, or, when the collateral is already submittable, the outcome of a `gobject submit` made within the request (`submitted` at 6 or more confirmations, `waiting` with `sent: true` below 6, `failed`, or `waiting` with a retry). The returned `id` (16 random bytes) is the only handle: there is no lookup by gov hash.

200.description: this proposal with this collateral is already stored; its current record

202.description: accepted and held (or submitted at once)

get.description: 501 `disabled` when the relay runs with PROPOSAL_SUBMIT=0. Records in a final state (`submitted`, `failed`) are deleted RETENTION_DAYS after they finished; the id is then unknown (404 `not-found`).

Hash.description: lowercase hex in display (RPC) byte order; uppercase is accepted in requests

VoteId.description: 16 random bytes; the handle for status and cancel

VoteStatus.description: `sending`: `voteraw` is in flight right now (a few seconds at most); the vote cannot be cancelled and ends as `broadcast`, back as `held` / `maybe-broadcast` (retry) or `failed`. `maybe-broadcast`: waiting to be sent again like `held`, but an earlier attempt may already have reached Core (voteraw got no answer, the relay restarted mid-call, or a broadcast vote never showed up and is re-sent); it can never be cancelled and never goes back to `held`. Clients must treat unknown statuses as non-final.

network.description: must equal the relay's CORE_NETWORK; it also selects the vote signature scheme (testnet: hash scheme, everything else: message scheme)

signal.description: other signal names are refused with `bad-vote`

time.description: the signed nTime, unix seconds; at most MAX_HOLD_S (default 40 days) ahead of the relay's clock

sig.description: base64 of the 65-byte compact signature (the `voteraw` vote-sig argument)

releaseAt.description: unix seconds. Default max(now, time - RELEASE_MARGIN_S). Must satisfy time - 3540 <= releaseAt <= time + 86400 and releaseAt <= now + MAX_HOLD_S
effective release time, unix seconds (never earlier than the submission)

sig.description: base64 of the 65-byte `signmessage` signature over the cancel message

broadcastAt.description: when Core last accepted the vote from this relay

confirmedAt.description: when the vote was seen in `gobject getcurrentvotes`

attempts.description: voteraw calls that were answered (not counting `too-often` waits)

nextAttemptAt.description: held and maybe-broadcast votes: the earliest time (unix s) the relay sends it; null in every other state

holdReason.description: held and maybe-broadcast votes: why it waits. `release-time`: the client-chosen release; `one-change-per-hour`: Core accepts one change per masternode, proposal and signal per hour; `core-time-limit`: Core refuses votes timed more than 1 h ahead; `retrying`: after an error (see `lastError`). null in every other state

sameAsCurrent.description: at submission, the masternode's current funding vote in Core had the same outcome: broadcasting this one only moves the timestamp (flagged, not dropped). null: Core could not be asked

lastError.description: a short code, never a raw Core message. While held (or `sending`): `too-often` (Core said voting too often), `hour-rule` (this relay broadcast a vote of the masternode on the proposal less than 1 h + 30 s ago), `future-limit` (the signed time is more than 1 h ahead of Core's clock), `unknown-proposal`, `core-error`, `not-visible` (re-broadcast pending). When failed: `obsolete`, `mn-gone`, `mn-banned`, `mn-not-valid`, `bad-signature`, `unknown-proposal`, `core-error`, `unconfirmed`

maybeSent.description: an attempt may have reached Core (voteraw got no answer, the relay restarted mid-call, or the vote was broadcast and re-sent because it did not show up). Stays true if the vote later fails, since it may still be on the network. Such a vote is never cancellable

proposalSubmit.description: false: PROPOSAL_SUBMIT=0, every proposal endpoint answers 501

proposalHold.description: this relay has POST /v1/proposals and GET /v1/proposals/{id} (held submission); absent on older relays

time.description: the `time` of the governance object (part of its hash)

dataHex.description: proposal JSON as hex, at most 512 bytes

govHash.description: computed by the relay with governanceObjectHash

postponed.description: submitted below 6 confirmations: Core relayed it and makes it a full object at 6 (until then its copy is in memory only)

ProposalId.description: 16 random bytes; the handle for GET /v1/proposals/{id} (deliberately not the gov hash)

ProposalStatus.description: `waiting`: the collateral is not ChainLocked with `minConfirmations` confirmations (nor 6 deep) yet, a retry is pending (`lastError`, `nextAttemptAt`), or, with `sent: true`, Core took it below 6 confirmations and the relay checks again at 6. `submitting`: `gobject submit` is in flight (seconds). `submitted` (Core has it as a full object) and `failed` are final. Clients must treat unknown statuses as non-final.

confirmations.description: the collateral's confirmations when the relay last asked Core, capped at 6

minConfirmations.description: MIN_COLLATERAL_CONFS: the relay submits at this depth once a ChainLock covers the block (at 6 without one)

sent.description: `gobject submit` returned the hash below 6 confirmations: Core relayed the proposal and makes it live at 6. Also true on a `submitted` record that went this way

lastError.description: a short code. While waiting: `core-error` (Core did not answer; retried 30 s doubling to 10 min), `core-syncing` (Core is not synced with the masternode network yet, retried the same way), `collateral-missing` (Core does not know the collateral right now), `collateral-reorg` (Core refused the collateral and it is no longer ChainLocked or deep enough). When failed: `expired` (end_epoch passed before it was sent), `collateral-missing` (unknown to Core for PROPOSAL_MISSING_S), `unconfirmed` (not sent within PROPOSAL_MAX_WAIT_S; a sent record never fails for this), `bad-collateral`, `core-rejected` (see `coreMessage`), `core-hash-mismatch` (`gobject submit` returned another hash)

coreMessage.description: only with `lastError` `core-rejected`: Core's refusal, trimmed to 200 characters

nextAttemptAt.description: waiting: when the relay looks at it next (unix s); null in every other state

submittedAt.description: the hour it became `submitted` (Core has it as a full object)
